the principal components analysis of the results of six lung function tests in 458 coal miners reduced the six measurements to three principal components.

the development of new methods for the detection and classification of abnormalities of lung function in a coalmining population.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have used a statistical technique to analyse a large number of lung function measurements made on a population of coalminers and to reduce these to a smaller number of principal components which represent the major aspects of lung function and which can be used to identify men with abnormal lung size and function, to classify types of abnormality, and to quantify these.
we have developed a method of identifying abnormal lung function and have used it to identify a group of younger miners with lung disease.

the technique of principal component analysis provides an efficient and sensitive method of detecting abnormal lung function, particularly in younger miners, and that it can be used to identify and quantify the different types of abnormality.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown that the principal components method can be used to identify and quantify different aspects and types of functional abnormalities, and that the method can identify more young men with abnormal lung functions than the traditional methods based on predicted values.
